use_case_name: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status

claims.content: Customer initiates the auction status view for a specific product item by entering the Product ID and clicking 'Go'.

The Customer wants to view the history of a specific product item, including its auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to view the history of a specific product item, including its auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information.

claims.content: If the search results in no matches, the system displays a 'No Results' page that includes a 'Search Tips' section advising to check for typos/misspellings, remove unnecessary words such as 'and', 'the', or 'a', try plural and singular forms of the word, use fewer or more generic keywords, and contact support if those tips fail.

missing_aspects: Evidence does not explicitly state that the Customer enters a Product ID and clicks 'Go' immediately prior to this step.

claims.content: The system displays the requested product item's current and past auction status in two sections: a top product summary section showing Product ID, description, product type, unit cost, price, thumbnail image, auction history stats/metrics, buyer's name, available quantity, and active date; and a bottom auction history section listing individual auction records on separate lines, each with Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount, High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The system displays current and past auction status details, including a Product Description/Specifications section (SKU, Type, Brand, Width, Metal Type, etc.) and an Item Bid History section listing Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User? for each bid.

Upon selecting 'Bid History' from the customer results list, the system displays a Bid History section in which each auction record shows the closing date/time (or 'Active' for live auctions), auction sequence number, Product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, SmartBid if placed, and the winning bid (regardless of who placed it).
Customer

Diverges from the main flow step where the Customer views bid history (the My Bid History page): If the Customer's default payment type is PayPal or Amazon Payments, the 'Payment Status' column for won items may show 'Not Paid' until the Customer has paid for their winnings.

Diverges from Step 2: If the Customer's default payment type is PayPal or Amazon Payments and the Customer has not yet paid for a won item, the 'Not Paid' status appears in bold red text and links to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page.
Diverges from Step 2: The page also includes a 'Recently Ended Auctions' link showing 24 hours of past auction history, providing an alternative viewing scope instead of the full bid history.
Diverges from Step 2: Under the search results, the Customer may click the 'Export to Excel' button to generate a CSV file of all data in the search results for manual tracking.
The user (Customer) has access to the SKU History page, where the system is ready to accept a Product ID to display the current and past auction status of a specific product item.
Customer enters the Product ID for the specific product item and clicks 'Go'.

The system displays the search results in two sections: a top product-summary section showing Product ID, Description, Type, Cost, Price, Thumbnail Image, Auction History stats, Buyer Name, Available Quantities, and Active Date; and a bottom auction-history section with records on separate lines.

In the bottom section, the system lists each auction record with Auction Status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount, High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The customer views the Product Details page for the specific product item, which includes a Product Description/Specifications section (SKU, Type, Brand, Width, Metal Type, etc.) and an Item Bid History section listing Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User status for each bid.

quality_flags.detail: [goal_mainflow_alignment] Goal claim names 'The Auctioneer (Administrator)' as the actor who wants to monitor auction status, but main_flow and the Primary Actor slot have the Customer entering a Product ID and viewing product/auction history. This conflates the Customer's self-service status view with an Auctioneer/Administrator monitoring use case, so the goal is not consistent with main_flow. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited card supports 'view the history', not an ongoing 'monitor' activity; no evidence for the added monitor wording.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Postcondition 3 describes a Bid History view reached by selecting 'Bid History' from the customer results list, with closing/active date/time, auction sequence, Product ID, customer's last bid, SmartBid, and winning bid. The main flow displays the search results and auction-history records (steps 2-3) and then moves to the Product Details page (step 4), but contains no step where the customer selects 'Bid History' or the system displays that Bid History section. Therefore the main flow does not reasonably lead to postcondition 3.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 2 says 'Diverges from Step 2', but main_flow Step 2 is the system displaying search results in product-summary and auction-history sections. The branch then discusses a 'Not Paid' payment status for a won item and a link to the Returning Winner's Payments page, which is not part of that search-results step and is not logically related to any existing main-flow step.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 1 says it diverges from the main-flow step where the Customer views bid history (the 'My Bid History page'), but main_flow Step 4 only has the Customer viewing the Product Details page's Item Bid History section. There is no 'My Bid History' page and no 'Payment Status' column for won items in main_flow, so this branch is not attached to an existing, logically matching main-flow step.

inconsistency_hints: The use case names Customer as the Primary Actor, and the Trigger/Main Flow describe a Customer entering a Product ID and clicking 'Go'. The only Precondition claim, however, asserts that the user is logged in as 'Auctioneer' and sees 'Welcome Back, Auctioneer!'. This creates a role conflict in the vertical flow: a Customer-triggered auction status lookup does not continue from an Auctioneer-specific login entry state.

Postconditions 2 and 3 require the system to display a Product Description/Specifications section and an Item Bid History section with per-bid fields such as Name, Amount, Date Placed, SmartBid User?, customer's last bid, SmartBid, and winning bid. The Main Flow only reaches a product-summary section and an auction-history record section; it does not include any step that opens or reveals the Product Description/Specifications or Item Bid History sections. The Main Flow's coverage_state claims MF-bid-history-selection and MF-bid-history-details are covered, but no Main Flow claim actually contains such steps, so those postconditions are not reasonably reached.

The goal claim identifies the actor as 'The Auctioneer (Administrator)', while the primary_actor slot and main_flow describe a Customer entering a Product ID and viewing auction/bid history. The goal statement conflates an Auctioneer/Administrator monitoring use case with the Customer-facing use case; the goal itself should be corrected to the Customer's goal.

The first alternative-flow branch (and the related second branch) is attached to Step 2, but the branch concerns a won-item 'Payment Status' column and a link to the Returning Winner's Payments page. Main flow Step 2 is the search-results/product-summary display for auction status; it has no payment-status/won-items context, and post-auction payment is outside the goal scope. The divergence point is therefore logically unrelated to Step 2.

Postcondition 3 asserts that the displayed Bid History section shows closing date/time (or 'Active'), auction sequence number, Product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, SmartBid if placed, and the winning bid for each auction record. The main flow only displays the bottom auction-history fields (Auction Status, Sequence, Start/End, Reserve, High Bid, Number of Bids, Winner/High Bidder) and an Item Bid History of Name/Amount/Date Placed/SmartBid User status. No upstream step establishes the customer-specific last-bid/SmartBid/winning-bid presentation promised by PC3, so this postcondition is not reachable from the described main flow.
